summary: Hugh Edward Richardson (1905–2000) was a Tibetologist who studied at Keble College, Oxford (~1924–1928). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1930–1947), founded the Tibet Society and the Institute of Tibetan Studies, and was a visiting professor at the University of Washington (~1961–1962).

Hugh Falconer (1808–1865) studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1822–1826) and University of Edinburgh (~1826–1829). He served as superintendent of Saharanpur Botanical Garden (1832), and later as superintendent of the Indian Botanic Garden and professor of botany at Calcutta Medical College (1848–1855).

Hugh George Rawlinson (1880–1957) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Emmanuel College (~1899–1903). His career included posts at the Ceylon Educational Service (1903), Karnatak Arts College (1917–1923), and Deccan College (~1919–1933).

Hugh Gray (1916–2002) worked in Indology and other fields after studying at Battersea Grammar School. He served as a lecturer at the University of London and held a post at SOAS University of London (~1960–1983).

Hugh J. Silverman (1945–2013) was a philosopher who earned his doctorate at Stanford University (~1969–1973). He was a professor at Stony Brook University from 1974 and served as executive director of the International Association for Philosophy and Literature (~1976–2013).

Hugh Trevor Lambrick (1904–1982) was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Oriel College (~1923–1927) and the University of Oxford (1971). He served as president of the Sind Historical Society (1940–1943) and fellow and lecturer at Oriel College.

Hugh van Skyhawk is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied under Günther-Dietz Sontheimer. Attested in 2008, he served as Professor of Comparative Religion in the Taxila Institute of Asian Civilizations at Quaid-i-Azam University.

Hugo David, an Indology and philosophy scholar, earned a PhD from the École Pratique des Hautes Études and studied under several traditional teachers. He held a fellowship at the University of Cambridge (2013–2014) and became a permanent member of the EFEO in 2015.

Hugo Ehrlich (1878–1914) was a linguist who studied at the University of Jena and the University of Leipzig under Karl Brugmann, earning his Ph.D. in 1901. In 1912, he was Privatdozent for Indo-European linguistics at the University of Königsberg.

Hugo Enomiya-Lassalle (1898–1990) was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied under traditional teacher Koun Yamada (~1968–1978) and held a post at Sophia University.

Hugo Heinrich Figulla (1885–1969) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Bruno Meissner at the University of Breslau (Ph.D. ~1907–1911). He held positions at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1934–1936) and the British Museum (1946–1963).

Hugo Schuchardt (1842–1927) was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Bonn under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl (~1861–1864). He held professorships of Romance philology at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1873) and the University of Graz (1876–1900).
Hugo Valvanne (1894–1961) was an Indology scholar who completed an M.A. at the University of Helsinki (~1912–1917), where he studied under J. N. Reuter.
Hugo Winckler (1863–1913) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1882–1886) and later held an academic post there (~1891–1913).
Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University, studying under supervisor Yi-hsun Huang (attested 2011).
Huifeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a student under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007) and held a post at the University of Hong Kong.

Huimin (born 1954) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1986–1992). He held posts at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, Taipei National University of the Arts, and served as president of Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (~2014–2022).
Huishan Lin is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Kuo-wei Liu, also studying under Mansheng, Miaoguan, and Ruying.
Huiwen Zhuang is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Kirill Solonin, and also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Huiyu Zhang (born 1951) works in the fields of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and served as a lecturer at Dongguk University (attested 1996).
